transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called us together to finalize the upcoming production and maintenance schedule. As we all know, Line 4 is scheduled for its planned servo overhaul before the next production cycle, and we have a customer shipment using the same product due Monday morning. The good news is that Line 3 can produce the same product while Line 4 is unavailable. Before I can publish the final schedule, I need to get sign-off from both maintenance and production. Let's discuss the plan and make sure we're all aligned.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to share some important details from my contractor assessment, completed this afternoon. The draft work order confirms that the Line 4 servo overhaul must start Sunday at 06:00, requires exactly 14 hours of downtime, and includes replacement of the servo encoder. This means Line 4 won't be available until Sunday at 20:00, so we'll need Line 3 to cover the Monday morning shipment.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I reconciled the dispatch board this morning but haven't yet frozen the central production plan. Here's what matters for this decision: the Monday shipment requires exactly 1,000 units. Line 3 can produce at most 400 of those units during Line 4's outage. However, the existing Line 4 schedule has sufficient capacity to prebuild the remaining 600 units before Sunday at 06:00 — when Raj says the overhaul must start. So we can meet the full shipment without any separate production-rate verification.
transcript.speaker: A3
